result:
No failures (the four warnings are pre-existing, about unrelated controllers lacking test files).

The excerpt was never lost from the database — it was being dropped one layer above it, in serialization. `PostResource.toArray()` (`app/Http/Resources/PostResource.ts`) built its payload from `id`, `title`, `body`, `authorId`, `createdAt` and `author`, skipping `excerpt` even though the `PostResourceData` interface right above it declares `excerpt: string`; because `toJSON()` casts through that interface, TypeScript never flagged the gap. Since every post-facing page reads the same resource, all three symptoms had this one cause: `posts/Index.tsx` and `Home.tsx` render `post.excerpt` on each card, `posts/Show.tsx` renders it between the byline and body, and `posts/Edit.tsx` seeds its form state from `post.excerpt` — so the field arrived `undefined` and the edit form posted an empty string, tripping "Excerpt is required.". Search kept working because it filters with a SQL `LIKE` against the `excerpt` column directly, never touching the serializer. I added the missing `excerpt: post.excerpt as string` line to `toArray()`, matching the surrounding style, and nothing else. I also added `tests/PostResource.test.ts`, a DB-free unit test that pins `excerpt` in the serialized output plus the other fields alongside it, so a future drop fails loudly. `bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` is 4 pass / 0 fail across 3 files (the 422 stack trace in the output is the pre-existing search test's expected validation error being logged).
